newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks scramble to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks scramble to higher close.

text.p: SPI futures 2291 +1 US 30yr cl 6.91 +0.02
*Stocks close higher, climb off lows as turnover picks up in afternoon ahead of futures expiry. Turnover 250.94 million, A$692.05 million value, 934 traded, 276 steady, 389 up, 269 down.
Australian shares closed firmer on Monday after the market scrambled off its lows in the afternoon ahead of the September share price index futures expiry.
At 4.10 p.m. (0610 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 7.4 points higher at 2290.40.
The September share price index was one point higher at 2291, a 0.6 point premium to the underlying index.
After a morning of treading water in a narrow range just under square, brokers said a spurt of activity in the leaders in the afternoon saw the bourse head to higher ground.
"Turnover picked up towards the end and that kept the run going but there were no dramatic moves," said a Sydney dealer.
The Australian market has now finished higher for the fifth consecutive day.
Noting that mining stocks closed at their lows, the dealer said some shuffling had occurred in the afternoon and pointed to CRA, BHP and WMC as stocks to watch on Tuesday.
"BHP and WMC were tossed around a bit and there could be some moves there tomorrow after trade settles." he said.
Among industrial stocks, the big banks found favour as buyers went looking for yield.
Other features remained elusive in a day where the focus was squarely on the leaders.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade was active as the September contract expired.
Options trade was slow, investors staying out as the market focussed on futures.
Total options traded 41,774
Turnover in September SPI contracts totalled 7,705

In other local markets, Australian short end bonds recovered to finish flat after a soft opening while the long bond remained below the key 91.21 level. Traders await the Reserve Bank of Australia meeting on Tuesday, and while most do not see a rate cut until November, the market is not prepared to rule one out.
By 5.30 p.m. (0730 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.82 percent, up 0.05 from Friday's levels.
The Australian dollar took advantage of yen weakness to push higher on Monday but could not completely shake off concerns of a possible rate cut this week.
By 5.30 p.m.(0730 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7927/32.
